sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Early County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Early County splits the job the way most rural Georgia counties do: the Early County Assessor's office values property, and the tax commissioner bills and collects. The county posts a Tax Commissioner Forms link on its forms and applications page. The assessor's office answers at (229) 723-3088, and the county administration office at 204 Court Square in Blakely answers at (229) 723-4304, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to noon and 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Parcel records live on qPublic under the Early County listing. Georgia's Revenue Department points owners to the tax commissioner for paying a bill, filing a homestead application and getting a copy of a bill, and to the assessor for appeals and the appraised value.

  • Value, appeal or property record: Early County Assessor.
  • Bill, payment and homestead forms: tax commissioner.
  • Which office takes a given form: ask the administration office in Blakely.

sections.h2: What is Early County like, and how does that shape its house values?
sections.html:
Early County lies in southwest Georgia, with Blakely as the county seat and Arlington, Damascus and Jakin as the other cities. Arlington is shared with Calhoun County. The county dates to 1818, and Calhoun, Clay, Decatur, Dougherty, Grady, Miller, Mitchell and Seminole counties were all carved out of its original territory.

Peanuts anchor the economy. The county's own history page calls Early the largest peanut quota holding county in the nation, and a peanut statue has stood on the square in Blakely since 1954. Kolomoki Mounds State Park holds a row of Native American mounds dating to around the year 800, and visitors also come for the Early County Museum and the Coheelee Creek Covered Bridge.

The Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied value of $131,300 across 4,993 housing units, and only 12 building permits were issued in 2025. Sellers here compete with a small supply of new homes.

sections.h2: What do Early County appraisal visits and notices involve?
sections.html:
Appraisal staff may visit any parcel between January 1 and December 31, and the county posts a standing notice under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 saying so. Visits can follow a return, an appeal, a site improvement permit, a homestead application, a conservation use application or a routine review. Staff gather property details and take photographs. If nobody is home, they leave a business card. They carry photo identification and drive a marked vehicle, and the assessor's office confirms a visitor's identity if you call.

The same notice reminds elderly owners that extra homestead exemptions exist on top of the regular one, and that you must apply by April 1 to receive an exemption. Read the full law for each exemption before you assume you qualify.

A May 2026 update from the Georgia Department of Revenue describes a revised Notice of Assessment under SB 566. The new notice is meant to carry details on exemptions and credits, an estimate of tax savings, a named contact for the appeal, a plain statement of fair market value, and a note that a homestead application can still be filed during the 45-day appeal window. It also tells owners to report homestead ineligibility by the end of that window, since the tax and a 50 percent penalty follow the property.

sections.h2: How do assessment appeals and homestead filing work in Early County?
sections.html:
An Early County owner who disagrees with a value has 45 days from the date the notice was mailed to file a written appeal with the Early County Assessor. Georgia uses one uniform appeal form, and the appeal may challenge taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption. On that form you pick the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator.

The Department of Revenue says it cannot override the assessors, the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, an arbitrator or Superior Court on an individual value. Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and the state's formula subtracts the homestead exemption from that assessed figure before applying the millage rate.

The same Revenue Department briefing says the HOME Act of 2026 ends the local opt-out from the HB 581 floating homestead exemption. Under that summary the statewide exemption starts on January 1, 2027 and counts 2026 values as its baseline, so a 2026 notice in Early County matters beyond that single tax year.

For homestead, the owner must have owned and lived in the home on January 1. File with the tax commissioner, or the assessor where the county has delegated it, by the property tax return deadline of April 1 or within the 45-day appeal window. Before you file, take these steps:

  • Keep the notice and note the mailing date on it.
  • Photograph defects and keep repair bids that justify a lower value.
  • Ask the assessor's office for the property record card before you file.
  • Ask which local exemptions Early County offers beyond the state's $2,000 standard exemption.

sections.h2: What do the Early County numbers look like?
sections.html:
Early County covers 512.6 square miles of land and holds about 21 people per square mile. The population estimate for July 1, 2025 was 10,455, down 3.7 percent from the 2020 base, and 22.6 percent of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: What should an Early County seller know about property tax at closing?
sections.html:
The owner on January 1 owes the full year's tax, and the Revenue Department says Georgia does not refund part of a year to someone who sells after that date. Property tax bills in most counties give 60 days to pay and are normally due December 20, though counties may differ. Ask the Early County tax commissioner for the billing date and the balance on your parcel.

Request a payoff figure from the tax commissioner before you sign a sale contract, and ask whether older years remain open. County tax liens that the commissioner issues are handled by that office, and filed liens sit on the general execution docket at the clerk.

A cash sale as-is can suit an Early County house that needs a roof, has tenants or carries back taxes, because the buyer takes the repairs and the tax balance is paid from proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Who values property in Early County, Georgia?
faqs.a: The Early County Assessor's office sets values and handles appeals, and you can reach it at (229) 723-3088. The tax commissioner is the office that bills and collects the tax.

faqs.q: Can Early County appraisers visit my house without notice?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's standing notice says appraisal staff may visit between January 1 and December 31 for returns, appeals, permits, homestead or conservation applications or a routine review. They carry photo ID, drive a marked vehicle and leave a business card if nobody is home.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an Early County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the notice of assessment was mailed. File the appeal in writing with the assessor, then choose a Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator.

faqs.q: When must I apply for an Early County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File by April 1 for the current year, or within the 45-day appeal window following a notice. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1 of that year.

faqs.q: Does selling in the spring cancel the Early County tax bill for that year?
faqs.a: No. The owner on January 1 is responsible for the whole year, and Georgia does not refund a partial year. Ask the tax commissioner for the balance and settle it at closing.
